description.narrative: The most significant expected project-level outcome is to increase the capacity of mobile networks in Kenya, resulting in improved access to quality connectivity for individuals and businesses. Beyond the project outcomes, IFC anticipates that its financing will deepen the competitiveness of the mobile tower market in Kenya by expanding shared infrastructure integrating green power solutions via competition channels.

The proposed transaction is a multi-currency senior debt financing of up to US$30 million, including an IFC A Loan of up to US$20 million and remaining to be mobilized from a B Lender/parallel lender for Atlas Tower Kenya (ATK or the Company), an IFC client since 2021. The funding will (i) enable ATK to build and operate new macro towers in Kenya, expanding its existing portfolio of 442 towers; (ii) support ATKs Green Power Program which involves the large-scale deployment of solar power, battery storage, and off-grid or hybrid energy solutions to help reduce dependence on grid electricity and diesel; and (iii) refinance existing indebtedness (Project). ATK is an independent telecommunications infrastructure company operating in Kenya under a build-to-suit (BTS) model. Established in 2018, ATK owns and operates a portfolio of 442 towers and manages the full tower lifecycle, including site identification, land leasing, permitting, construction, energy solutions, and operations and maintenance.
